cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I told the committee I couldn't chair another year. Please appreciate what those two sentences took.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Could you stay on until we find someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I rehearsed in your car until I stopped apologising. That wasn't me advertising a temporary vacancy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't supply the excuse I spent an hour removing. Could you recognise a refusal I finally managed without one?

mechanism: A corrects its former pupil boundary-setting response to make it recognize the courage in A own unqualified refusal.
confusable: Not simply repeating no: A asks B to preserve and acknowledge refusal without inventing an excuse that erases the effort.
comparison: Edited anger versus clear departure from duty.
seedUse: D105 committee/refusal/car/rehearsal/exhaustion; S05 no-excuse teaching now applied to former teacher.
